title: Server-side rendering and hydration with Angular SSR

videos.script:
Until now, the planner's server has sent an empty page, and the browser has built every word of it. This lesson renders the page on the server first.

{{empty}} With JavaScript turned off, the planner shows nothing at all. That is what a slow phone shows while it waits, and what some search engines read.

{{add}} One command adds server-side rendering, and it loosens four versions on the way, so the lesson pins them back.

{{modes}} Each route can be rendered at build time, on every request, or only in the browser. The planner's data changes all day, so every request it is.

{{hydration}} The browser then takes over the page it was sent instead of drawing it again. It does not even ask for the data a second time.

{{server}} And the server is not a browser: there is no local storage there, and no focus. The preferences service learns to tell the two apart.

{{status}} A rendered page is also an answer with a status code. Two addresses said two hundred when they meant not found.

{{hosts}} Last, the production server. It refuses requests for names it does not know, and the reason is a kind of attack.
